basis: Written from the published specification and established practice in the field; no new sources were read. Unreviewed.

distinguishingFeatures: One award to one person, not the credential scheme that defines it.
Differs from a right to practise, which a regulator grants and which can be restricted separately.
Differs from a verifiable credential envelope, which is one way to present the award.
Status must be checked against the issuer; a document copy does not show current standing.

may: Record an award assertion with issuer and scheme references.
Record a status observation with source and time.
Remind the holder of renewal or continuing education deadlines.
Export a minimized projection for verification.
mustNot: Treat a valid signature or local record as current good standing.
Treat unknown or stale status as valid.
Issue, revoke or suspend a real credential.
Disclose disciplinary details beyond what the public register permits.
Advise on legal eligibility to practise.

considerations: Relying on a lapsed licence can put patients, clients or the public at risk.
Disciplinary data can harm careers if shown out of context or after it is spent.
Recognition barriers can unfairly exclude migrants with valid foreign qualifications.

items: An award has a holder reference, issuing body, scheme, award identifier, issue date and status.
Confused with academic degrees, training certificates, memberships and the right to practise.
Unqualified practice due to missed suspension.
Privacy harm from overshared disciplinary details.
